title: How Gypsies Work
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss the Romani (Roma) people, whom they note are often called "gypsies," a term they say they try to avoid as an ethnic slur. They cover the Roma's dispersal across Europe and forced movement, current discrimination in France, Italy, Britain and elsewhere, the theory of Indian origins (with Sanskrit found in the language and genetic testing), the migration via Persia and Turkey, enslavement in Romania (including Vlad Dracula owning Romani people), the Roma Holocaust (Porajmos) under the Nazis, the origin of the name "gypsy" from a mistaken belief they came from Egypt (via "Little Egypt"), Romani trades and music, social structure and arranged marriage, health and education disparities, the 1971 World Romani Congress and the push for recognition, and a listener mail segment about time travel questions.

segments.title: Opening banter and the term 'gypsy'
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about the show Jack & Mr. Sister-like references and a song, then discuss why they will avoid the word 'gypsy' as a pejorative, linked to the word 'jipped,' and mention Shel Silverstein's poem changed from 'The Gypsies Are Coming' to 'The Googies.'

segments.title: Roma today and European discrimination
segments.summary: They introduce the Roma as a dispersed population of about twelve million who are often forced to move. Discussion covers the 2013-2014 Paris evictions, the Roma as targets across the EU, a Rome camp removal, and the Gypsy Kings, who are of Romani descent from Spain.

segments.title: Origins in India and migration
segments.summary: The hosts explain that the Roma claim Indian origin, supported by Sanskrit in their language identified by an eighteenth-century Hungarian scholar and by genetic testing. They discuss a group displaced from northern India by raids around 1000 CE, moving through Persia and Turkey.

segments.title: Slavery in Romania and Vlad the Impaler
segments.summary: The Roma moved across the Balkans and were enslaved in Romania for about four centuries until abolition. Vlad the Impaler (Vlad Dracula) owned some Romani people. Discussion covers continued discrimination in Romania.

segments.title: Roma Holocaust (Porajmos)
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Nazi persecution of the Roma, with roughly half a million killed, the term Porajmos, and the lack of prosecution and mention at Nuremberg. They also mention a documentary on the Romani Holocaust.

segments.title: Origin of the name 'gypsy'
segments.summary: The hosts explain the name came from a mistaken belief the Roma were from Egypt, after some Roma settled in the Peloponnese area where a region called Little Egypt was located.

segments.title: Culture, social structure, health, and education
segments.summary: They discuss Romani trades and music, the men-dominated clan structure with women running households, arranged marriages, low literacy, high infant mortality and shorter life expectancy, and reliance on homeopathic medicine. They also note the Roma were fired first after communism.

segments.title: World Romani Congress and assimilation
segments.summary: They describe the 1971 World Romani Congress, which picked a flag and anthem and gained United Nations recognition as an ethnic group seven years later, and debate assimilation versus preserving identity, comparing the Chinese and Jewish middleman minority examples.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Closing remarks and a note that the Roma article is among their more confusing episodes, with a plug for the website.
